items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: Frank Foster. At any rate they had like three mics on stage.

ctx.x: Well that’s why when I listen to the Basie, they call it the All American Rhythm Section, it just sounds like one entity. Because they, I don’t know if they were so totally conscious of balancing their own volume but they surely did. And I had the experience once, on multiple, this one night after the other at a festival I heard the L.A. Juggernaut Big Band, Frankie Capp and Nat Pierce. And they had mics all over the place and it blew your head off. The next night the Count Basie Orchestra led by Grover Mitchell…
Frank Foster. At any rate they had like three mics on stage. And it was so much better. The band was in control rather than —

And they mixed themselves. When studio players, when I was playing sessions, and we would go out to play gigs with some artist or something, they’d pay to have us come out with them. We could mix ourselves from stage. We were so used to knowing what we sounded like in our headphones in the studio, once we were on the stage we knew exactly — we had our own levels set. They put the mics up but there was not a lot of mixing going on at the console out front. We mixed ourselves. Of course those guys, these are…
